$why: The COORDINATOR_PROMPT_AMENDMENT chain: text prepended to a writer's next attempt saying what went wrong last time. Four distinct situations, four bodies -- turns exhausted with the files already present, turns exhausted with nothing written, a defect escalated from a sibling story, and a deterministic check that failed.
The first two differ in one consequential way: whether the deliverable already exists. Told the wrong one, a writer either rewrites files it should read, or reads for files that were never created.

One body carried a whole conditional SECTION inside a ${VAR:+...} expansion -- the prior failure-analyst diagnosis, re-injected for context. Whether the writer saw it was decided by a parameter expansion, which is not a place anyone reads prompt text.
description: What a writer is told about the previous attempt when its next one is prepared.

bodies.turns_exhausted_files_exist: CRITICAL: The previous attempt exhausted all available turns without creating the required deliverable. These files already exist — their real content is injected in ## Existing File Contents; do not spend turns re-reading them. Use Edit for a targeted, minimal change and act on it immediately — do not re-explore the codebase beyond what's already injected.
bodies.turns_exhausted_nothing_written: CRITICAL: The previous attempt exhausted all available turns without creating the required deliverable. Your FIRST action MUST be to call WriteFile to the exact absolute path listed under 'Files to Create/Modify' — do NOT read files, do NOT plan, do NOT investigate. Write the required file IMMEDIATELY as your very first action.
bodies.sibling_escalation:
## URGENT: Escalated defect from sibling story __ESCALATING_STORY_ID__
__DIAGNOSIS__
Required fix: __REQUIRED_FIX__
Apply ONLY this fix to __TARGET_FILE__. Do not make any other changes to this file or any other file — this is a narrow, targeted patch, not a full re-implementation.
bodies.deterministic_check:
__EXISTING_AMENDMENT__
## Deterministic Check Failure
__VERIFICATION_FAILURE__
This was caught by an automated check before the test suite even ran — fix the exact issue named above.__PRIOR_DIAGNOSIS_SECTION__
